messages:
lia: Heads-up — since the microbatch change last night we're seeing p99 tail spikes on the 8xA100 pool for long-chat models. latency SLOs still OK p95 but p99 up ~2.8x. attaching quick profile below.

pranay: ack. saw the alert. any obvious kernel fallbacks in the traces?

lia: yes — profiler shows more frequent fallback to the generic attention kernel at sequence lengths >1024, plus KV cache misses when prefixes are longer. here's the hot log: 
```
[2026-06-12T02:11:05Z] model=redwood-2-l base_kernel=fast_attn_v2 used_kernel=generic_attn seq=1400 gpu_util=91% batch=3 latency=420ms
[2026-06-12T02:11:06Z] model=redwood-2-l kv_cache_hit=false prefix_tokens=850 microbatch_size=1
[2026-06-12T02:11:06Z] p99_window=1m 99th=880ms 95th=210ms
```

kevin: hmm. high util + fallback = long-tail. two levers: reduce microbatch to keep headroom or increase headroom admission threshold. which do we want?

sam: My vote: adaptive microbatching per-model. if seq_len_hist[model].p90 > 512 then prefer smaller microbatches, otherwise pack. simplest heuristic: target p95 <= SLO_margin and keep GPU util target 70-80% for long-chat models.

pranay: is there data on how KV cache misses correlate with microbatching? I thought larger microbatches amortize kernel overhead and reduce cost.

lia: they do for short sequences. For long prefixes, the KV cache lookup cost and memory pressure cause extra copies and sometimes force different memory layout -> kernel mismatch. So larger microbatches can push the runtime into a slower codepath for long-seq requests.

kevin: can we sketch adaptive admission pseudocode?

lia: sure — rough idea:
```
# per-model state: seq_hist, recent_p99, util_est
on_request(req):
  est_seq = percentile(seq_hist, 80)
  if est_seq > 1024 or util_est > 85%:
    microbatch_target = 1
  elif est_seq > 512:
    microbatch_target = 2
  else:
    microbatch_target = max_batch_for_latency(SLO - headroom)
  route_with_microbatch(microbatch_target)
```

sam: +1. also add KV-prefetch hint: if prefix_tokens > 512 set kv_prefetch=true so cache warms earlier. that reduced cold-miss spikes in my local tests.

pranay: how about admission control thresholds? current system uses 90% util to start shedding. maybe that's too aggressive for tail SLOs. we should consider a headroom buffer that's workload-aware (e.g., keep 15% headroom for long chat).

kevin: agree. typically we optimize cost by pushing util to 90%, but that removes headroom for tail events. For latency-first customers we should target 65-75% and for best-cost target 85-92%. need per-customer policy.

ops-bot: deploybot: rolled back microbatching 3 hours ago for trial group A. Observed p99 dropped from 860ms -> 320ms in that cohort. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

lia: nice — that rollback confirms microbatch change is a big factor. we still need a long-term fix: either smarter kernel selection (avoid fallback), or adaptive batch+admission.

pranay: kernel side: we can add a fast path for seq in [1024..1536] tuned to current GPU memory layout. but that needs testing and might increase code complexity.

sam: tradeoffs: invest in new kernels (engineering cost, but permanent) vs adaptive runtime heuristics (faster rollout, more brittle). lean towards runtime heuristics short-term, kernel optimization medium-term.

kevin: ops question — how do we validate per-model microbatch heuristics won't regress throughput and cost too much? need a rollout plan: A/B with traffic-shaping and track tokens/sec + p99 + cost/tokens.

lia: plan: 1) revert globally for now (done), 2) implement adaptive microbatch & kv_prefetch for cohort rollout, 3) instrument headroom metric and per-pool util target, 4) parallel kernel proto for long-seq paths.

pranay: add a gating eval: run full-profile on a subset of samples (seq lengths sampled) to ensure no unexpected kernel fallbacks.

kevin: also add alerting: if p99 increases >1.5x while tokens/sec stable -> auto-scale headroom (temporarily reduce admission until kernel patch).

lia: sg. I'll create an RFC with rollouts and the pseudocode + perf benchmarks. tagging @perfbot for baseline traces.

perfbot: perfbot: uploaded comparative traces to https://redwood-internal/perf/traces/17770023 (contains cohort A rollback traces + current main).

sam: thanks. thumbs-up on the staged approach. :thumbsup:

kevin: timeline? can we ship heuristics in 2 sprints?

lia: yes — aim for initial adaptive runtime rollout in 2 sprints, kernel proto in 4. I'll open PRs tonight for telemetry and the microbatch flag.

pranay: ok. I'll own the headroom alert rule and synthetic tests.

lia: thanks everyone. we'll sync in the runtime standup tomorrow.

kevin: ack.
